waves.name: Batch environment and file bracket jobs
waves.rationale: Seventeen units that run no application program and, on the facts the extractor could read, touch no shared data: the CICS file close and open jobs, the GDG base definitions, catalog, RACF and CICS definition utilities, two test data builders and six scheduler entries. It is a sound first wave because it proves build, deploy and rollback at no business risk. It is not empty of consequence: DEFGDGB and DALYREJS define the GDG bases that waves 4 and 5 write generations into, and CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL are the only thing that keeps batch and online off the same VSAM, so they stay in the legacy scheduler until wave 6 ends. Six units the seed put here were moved out (see deviations): three DB2 jobs and two of their scheduler entries to wave 7, and TRANIDX to wave 5.
waves.unblocks: The toolchain, the new scheduler, and the GDG base definitions that waves 4 and 5 write under. Beyond that it is a chore.

waves.name: Read only master extracts
waves.rationale: Batch programs that read the four masters and write files nobody else uses. This is the cheapest place to prove that the target reads the legacy record layouts CVACT01Y, CVACT02Y, CVACT03Y and CVCUS01Y byte for byte. READACCT writes three copies of the account master in three formats, so it doubles as a golden master generator. CBIMPORT sits here by the seed rule, but its job defines no CARDOUT DD, so it cannot open its outputs as written: fix or drop it before counting it as a working baseline.
waves.unblocks: The layout proof for the masters that waves 5 and 6 write, and the first oracle files for the harness.

waves.name: Sign on, menu and read only screens
waves.rationale: COSGN00C, COMEN01C and COADM01C are one strongly connected component, so they move together as the front door. They dispatch every option through the tables in COMEN02Y and COADM02Y, so this wave needs a router facade that hands each option whose program is not yet ported back to legacy CICS. The other five are read only screens (COACTVWC, COCRDSLC, and the COTRN00C and COTRN01C pair) plus the date check CSUTLDTC that waves 5 and 6 also call. The wave reads masters that batch and online writers in waves 5 and 6 still own, so it reads through a data access facade until then. COSGN00C compares a clear text password, so the wave carries a credential decision. Low-high units go early only once the harness from wave 2 works.
waves.unblocks: The front door, the router that every later online wave plugs into, and the shared date check.

waves.name: Reference data loads and build tooling
waves.rationale: Jobs that reload reference and secondary files (DISCGRP rates, TRANTYPE and TRANCATG descriptions, CUSTFILE, DUSRSECJ, TRANFILE) plus nine units of compile tooling that the target build replaces, so the real port is smaller than the count. The four high-high master reload jobs the seed put here were moved to waves 5 and 6 (see deviations). Every dataset direction in this wave comes from DISP only, because the IDCAMS and SORT control cards are not read, so read and write here are guesses until the client confirms them. TRANTYPE and TRANCATG reload from flat files that the DB2 unload TRANEXTR writes in wave 7, so that unload has to keep running unchanged.
waves.unblocks: The interest rate table CBACT04C reads and the type and category tables CBTRN03C reads, so wave 5 can be tested against loaded reference data.

waves.name: Daily posting cycle, interest, transaction report and statements
waves.rationale: One temporal chain: POSTTRAN, INTCALC, TRANBKP, COMBTRAN and TRANIDX, bracketed by CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL. It has one boundary that can be tested: the transaction, account and category balance masters after the cycle. The transaction report (CBTRN03C, its job, its proc and the online request in CORPT00C) is here because it reads that master and the online request runs the same proc. ACCTFILE, TCATBALF and XREFFILE come here because this wave holds the first programs that write or validate against those files, so the system of record flips here. Sixteen units are high-high. The wave is in the second half, and it cannot be later because waves 6 and 7 read what it writes. It needs a facade: a scheduler shim that starts the ported POSTTRAN when the legacy CBPAUP0J ends, because CA-7 lists CBPAUP0J as the job that triggers POSTTRAN, until wave 7 moves CBPAUP0J. Strangle each high-high program behind a facade with a shadow run; do not port it in one cut.
waves.unblocks: The nightly cycle on the target. It ends the delete and redefine of the transaction master and lets wave 6 write online without CLOSEFIL.

waves.name: Online maintenance writers
waves.rationale: Online programs that write the shared masters: COACTUPC (3,368 lines, 43 REDEFINES), COCRDUPC, COBIL00C, COTRN02C, the four user maintenance programs, and COCRDLIC, which hands off to COCRDUPC. CARDFILE and the full batch wrapper come here because the card master's first writer, COCRDUPC, is here. This wave ends the online and batch sharing of VSAM, so CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL can be retired after it. It carries the largest program by size and the hardest concurrency change: today the only thing between COACTUPC and CBTRN02C on the account master is the close and open bracket.
waves.unblocks: Retirement of the CICS VSAM files and of CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL; every writer of the four masters is on the target.

waves.name: IMS, DB2 and MQ subsystem
waves.rationale: Everything that touches IMS, DB2 or MQ, including five programs and three DB2 jobs that the extractor could not see as edges because the JCL names them in a PARM or in TSO input. The plugin does not read DBDs, PSBs, DDL or DCLGEN, so this is the least understood wave. It holds 14 high-high units, and it is last because nothing else depends on it except CBPAUP0J, which triggers POSTTRAN in CA-7, and the weekly DB2 unload that feeds the transaction type files. Both keep running in legacy until this wave, behind the wave 5 shim and the wave 4 dependency.
waves.unblocks: Retirement of IMS, DB2 and MQ, and of the last scheduler dependency of the posting job.

unassigned.reason: No JCL step names it and no reachable code calls it by name. It only verifies daily transactions and writes nothing. Kept in the unknown bucket; see dead-code.json.

deviations.reason: The program builds JCL text that runs proc TRANREPT and writes it to the JOBS queue. That job runs CBTRN03C, a wave 5 unit and the must-not-break transaction report. Moving CORPT00C to wave 5 keeps the online request and the report in one test boundary.
Named inside JCL text in CORPT00C and it runs CBTRN03C. The extractor makes no edge for it, so the seed left it unplaced. It moves with CBTRN03C.
The job runs COBTUPDT with a DB2 plan through TSO. The extractor cannot see that, so it counted the job as a utility. Anything that touches DB2 belongs in wave 7.
Follows job MNTTRDB2.
Run by MNTTRDB2 through TSO RUN PROGRAM. No call edge exists, so the seed left it unplaced. It moves with its job.
The job unloads DB2 with DSNTIAUL and writes the TRANTYPE and TRANCATG flat files. The extractor does not resolve &HLQ, so it saw no dataset and no DB2 use.
Follows job TRANEXTR.
Creates DB2 objects through DSNTIAD. It touches DB2, so it belongs in wave 7.
The job CBPAUP0J names it in a BMP PARM. No call edge exists, so the seed left it unplaced. It moves with its job.
Named in the PARM of UNLDGSAM. It moves with its job.

Daily posting is a must-not-break item and it is one chain: POSTTRAN, INTCALC, TRANBKP, COMBTRAN. TRANBKP deletes and redefines the master that POSTTRAN opens for output. Split across waves, the wave 4 boundary could not be tested without wave 5 output.
Its input is the SYSTRAN generation that INTCALC writes. It is the last step of the posting cycle and shares its test boundary.
Follows job TRANBKP.
Follows job COMBTRAN.

TRANBKP deletes the transaction alternate index and TRANIDX rebuilds it right after POSTTRAN and COMBTRAN in every wrapper. The BLDINDEX control card reads the shared master, and control cards are not read.

High-high and must-not-break. It is the last wave that does not break a dependency: CBTRN02C and CBACT04C, the first programs to write the account master, are in wave 5, and the system of record flips there.
High-high. CBTRN02C is its first writer and moves in wave 5.
High-high. No program writes the cross reference, and its first dependent programs, CBTRN02C and CBACT04C, are in wave 5.
High-high and must-not-break. The card master's first writer, COCRDUPC, is in wave 6, so the system of record flips there.
